rationale_evidence.anchor: Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.
rationale_evidence.statement: Zero-Lens result on Williamson: after removing beliefs, documents, language, databases, probabilities, possible worlds, embeddings, topics, LLMs, what survives is minimal: 'A participant is related to a proposition/content in a world/context/time such that the proposition is true and the participant is in a factive state of knowing.' Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 1. Participants make commitments. 2. Commitments have inferential consequences. 3. Some commitments are supported/entitled...
rationale_evidence.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brandom (removing language/English/sentences/speech/Frege/Wittgenstein/philosophy) yields ten survivor claims: participants make commitments; commitments have inferential consequences; some commitments are supported/entitled; commitments can conflict; participants assess one another's commitments; new actions alter the state; implicit relations can become explicit; concepts are characterized partly by inferential roles; objectivity can emerge within social assessment; a claim is not merely a string but a position in a normative/inferential structure.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 1. There is an underlying world/domain. 2. A participant has beliefs/knowledge about it. 3. Only part of that knowledge may be explicitly represented...
rationale_evidence.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brachman & Levesque (removing FOL/Prolog/frames/description logic/SAT/default logic/Bayesian networks/STRIPS/GOLOG) yields twelve survivor claims: an underlying world/domain exists; a participant has beliefs/knowledge about it; only part is explicitly represented; representation is a mapping between domains; reasoning derives implicit content from explicit content; meaning depends on interpretation/context; different representation languages have different expressive power; reasoning capability is resource-limited; knowledge changes and can be revised; uncertainty/vagueness require richer representations; the same knowledge may have different representations; action depends on knowledge — described as extraordinarily close to the current model.

rationale_evidence.anchor: what survives across *both* phases is: **a knower/participant · something known · a ground · and a record that the two were connected.**
rationale_evidence.statement: Zero-Lens applied across both phases: after stripping optional attributes, what survives universally is a knower/participant, something known, a ground, and a record that the two were connected — every phase and nearly every model retains those four; nothing else survives universally. The corpus distinguishes 'nothing exists' from 'we do not know' (0258: 'Knowledge is not only about what exists'; formal law §9: unknown≠absent≠false). Whether UNKNOWN is the absence of Knowledge or a state of an identified object is NOT resolved by the corpus: formal law (⟨Z-1⟩) says UNKNOWN/ABSENT/FALSE/REJECTED are states of an identified epistemic object, while kernel document 125708 §17 pushes the other way ('UNKNOWN must not be a single epistemic state', eight readings) — no new state proposed here.

rationale_evidence.anchor: ALT-05 · Zero as absence-lens primitive
rationale_evidence.statement: Zero as the epistemology of absence (Vedic-zero lens era, 20260822-103624) was, inside the formal track, transformed into the goal-gap function (CON-01); on the repository side the sibling sense was instead RATIFIED as meta-principle Z-KOS-001 — resulting in the three-sense Zero naming collision, a live naming hazard for Final Architecture.

sources.note: Step 152/153's machine-readable Architecture Registry declaring bounded contexts/aggregates/dependencies/ports/adapters/contracts/rules/invariants, with an ArchitectureRule schema, severity levels, a governed-exception mechanism, and worked conformance-check examples comparing declared vs implemented architecture.

rows.anchor: domain/ MUST NOT import web/, persistence/, adapters/, vendor/ — automatable static analysis.
rows.statement: Presents the module dependency graph (API->Application->{Domain,Ports}<-Adapters) as particularly suitable for deterministic static-analysis enforcement.

rows.anchor: architecture-registry/{bounded-contexts, aggregates, dependencies, ports, adapters, contracts, rules, invariants}. ArchitectureRegistry defines what is allowed; code provides what exists; assurance compares them.
rows.statement: Proposes the existing KnowledgeOS registry concept become the machine-readable source of declared-architecture rules, distinct from and comparable against the actual code.

rows.anchor: ArchitectureConformance = DeclaredArchitecture =? ImplementedArchitecture. A deterministic verification problem.
rows.statement: Formalizes architecture conformance as a comparison problem, worked with three concrete FAIL examples: (1) registry says domain.assurance may depend only on itself/ports/shared-kernel, but assurance/Rule.java imports nexus.NexusClient -> FAIL; (2) registry says Action requires Authorization, but runtime shows Action->Execute with no authorization reference -> FAIL; (3) registry says Verification requires RuleVersion+EvidenceReference, but the implementation's Verification only has ruleId without version -> FAIL — 'this is where architecture becomes machine-checkable.'

rows.anchor: ArchitectureRule{ruleId,category,scope,predicate,severity,checker,remediation}. Severity: BLOCKING/ERROR/WARNING/ADVISORY. Violation + ApprovedException does not become NoViolationEverOccurred.
rows.statement: Defines the ArchitectureRule schema and severity taxonomy, worked example ARCH-DOM-001 (domain_must_not_depend_on_adapter, severity=BLOCKING); defines the architecture-exception mechanism (Architecture Rule->Violation->{no exception->BLOCK, valid exception->permitted}) as a governed connection back to the Governance model, with the invariant that an approved exception modifies applicability but never erases the historical violation.

rows.anchor: Evidence{source=ArchitectureChecker, subject=repository-X, rule=ARCH-DOM-001, observedAt, result=PASS} referenced by Verification. Architecture Constitution → Architecture Registry → Implementation → Deterministic Checker → Evidence → Verification → Finding → Governance/Exception — essentially KnowledgeOS applied to itself.
rows.statement: Requires every architecture check to produce evidence in the same model as engineering assurance, and assembles the architecture-assurance loop, described as 'essentially KnowledgeOS applied to itself.'

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS must be capable of verifying conformance to its own architectural constitution (not necessarily from v0.1, but as the target). ARCH-DOM-001, ARCH-DOM-002, ARCH-API-001, ARCH-AUTH-001, ARCH-ASSURE-001, ARCH-EVID-001, ARCH-TRACE-001, ARCH-AGENT-001.
rows.statement: States the self-hosting principle (self-verification of the architecture's own constitution) and lists eight initial machine-checkable ARCH-nnn rules to automate first (domain dependency direction, no external DTO in domain, no direct arbitrary state mutation, action requires authorization, verification requires exact rule version, verification references evidence, material operation has TraceID, agent cannot bypass authorization).

rows.anchor: Commit → Build → Architecture Checks → Deterministic Assurance → Tests → Package (CI, blocking on violation). pre-commit → fast architecture checks (local). Agent → change code → run architecture assurance → PASS/FAIL.
rows.statement: Defines three enforcement points (CI, local pre-commit, agent harness) all running the same architecture checks.

rows.anchor: Observe → Reason → Change → Verify → Correct, with KnowledgeOS supplying the Verify stage. Agent may be autonomous in Reasoning/CodeGeneration; not autonomous in GovernanceAuthority.
rows.statement: States the critical AI-engineering agent loop and restates the agent-autonomy boundary — deterministic/platform-controlled governance authority remains outside agent autonomy regardless of reasoning/codegen freedom.

rows.anchor: What contexts, modules, aggregates, dependencies, ports, adapters, contracts and rules does KnowledgeOS actually declare? DeclaredArchitecture vs ActualRepository.
rows.statement: Opens Step 153 (KnowledgeOS Architecture Registry): defines the Registry as the missing link between Constitution and Implementation, enabling the first real deterministic architecture assurance by comparing declared architecture against the actual repository.

rows.anchor: Registry ≠ Database (what MAY exist vs what DOES exist). Registry ≠ Constitution (Constitution: 'a domain module MUST NOT depend on an adapter'; Registry: assurance.allowedDependencies=[assurance,shared-kernel,ports]; Implementation: assurance imports nexus-adapter; Verification: ARCH-DOM-001 FAIL).
rows.statement: Establishes the Registry as a machine-readable declaration of intended architecture (contexts, modules, aggregates, ports, adapters, APIs, events, dependencies, persistence ownership, rules, checkers — no runtime business data) and gives the complete worked assurance chain distinguishing it from both the database and the Constitution.

rows.anchor: architecture-registry/{contexts,modules,aggregates,concepts,ports,adapters,contracts,events,persistence,dependencies,rules,metadata}. registry{id,version,status,effectiveFrom}, potentially approvedBy/approvedAt/supersedes.
rows.statement: Specifies the Registry's top-level directory structure (format-agnostic) and its own identity/versioning metadata.

rows.anchor: contexts{governance:BC-GOV, knowledge:BC-KNOW, evidence:BC-EVID, assurance:BC-ASSURE, agent:BC-AGENT, action:BC-ACTION, authorization:BC-AUTH}, each with status CANDIDATE|CONFIRMED|DEPRECATED|RETIRED — the final context list must align with the approved Architecture Landscape, not be invented by implementation.

rows.statement: Specifies dependency declarations and argues allowlists are safer than enumerating forbidden dependencies for critical boundaries, since a new/unlisted dependency automatically fails rather than silently passing.

rows.anchor: aggregates{action:{context,root,consistencyBoundary:local}, verification:{...}}, with per-aggregate invariants (e.g. authorization-required-before-execution, action-id-immutable) that the checker can verify have corresponding tests — Architecture → Executable Assurance.

A checker using an LLM for interpretation is deterministic:false and cannot silently serve as an authoritative deterministic verifier. Rules also declare scope (appliesTo:layer/modules) to prevent overly broad checking.

rows.anchor: NoDuplicateContextID, NoUnknownOwner, NoCircularForbiddenDependency, EveryPortHasOwner, EveryAdapterImplementsDeclaredPort — the Registry itself must be validated before implementation starts.

rows.anchor: ObservedArchitecture from scanning directories/packages/imports/APIs/events/dependencies. Compare(Declared,Observed) is the central conformance operation.
rows.statement: Defines implementation discovery (repository scan producing ObservedArchitecture) and the core conformance comparison, worked with a per-category conformance result example (Contexts PASS, Modules PASS, Dependencies FAIL, APIs PASS, Events PASS, Persistence ownership PASS) — 'significantly stronger than a human architecture review alone.'

rows.anchor: Six months later someone adds a forbidden dependency; CI detects ArchitectureDrift. Code Change → Architecture Scanner → Observed Architecture → Compare Registry → {CONFORM, DRIFT → Finding}.
rows.statement: Defines the same conformance mechanism applied continuously to detect post-implementation drift, turning architecture governance into an ongoing CI process, with a Finding schema (findingId, ruleId, subject, observedState, expectedState, evidenceId, severity) and worked example.

rows.anchor: A Finding may carry a remediationHint (e.g. 'introduce NexusPort and move vendor dependency into NexusAdapter') that AI can generate, but the Finding itself is generated deterministically — not 'AI says architecture looks fine.'
rows.statement: States the correct division between deterministic checker (produces the Finding) and AI (proposes remediation), and assembles the agent self-correcting remediation loop (Agent->Change->Architecture Check->{PASS->continue, FAIL->Finding->Agent->Correct}), 'where KnowledgeOS becomes an engineering feedback system.'

rows.anchor: Finding → Exception Request → Governance Decision → Approved Exception, with exception{rule,subject,expiresAt,approvedBy} scope. Violation+ValidException⇒Allowed; Violation+ExpiredException⇒FAIL.
rows.statement: Specifies the architecture-exception mechanism with explicit expiry evaluation, giving the Registry temporal semantics — architecture is A(t), not a static A, depending on active version/effective date/exceptions/migrations, important for historical audit.

Never allowedDependencies:'*' — the Registry must make architectural intent more explicit, not less.
rows.statement: States the Registry should be version-controlled with its own change-governance lifecycle and warns against using wildcard allowlists to bypass the purpose of the Registry.

rows.statement: Defines a six-category drift taxonomy for the Registry (first four especially important) and a worked architecture-assurance-result example (47 PASS, 1 WARNING, 0 BLOCKING) stored as Evidence->Verification->Finding, making architecture itself part of the KnowledgeOS assurance model.

rows.statement: Recasts Yoga's eight limbs (progressing from bodily/personality refinement toward senses, mind, higher consciousness) as a transformation lens for KnowledgeOS: Governance discipline -> Knowledge structural discipline -> Noise reduction -> Focused investigation -> Continuous reasoning -> Integrated understanding, described as closer to the project's existing knowledge workflow.

rows.anchor: K + provenance(K) + uncertainty(K) + authority(K) ... a reflexive knowledge system additionally represents K + provenance + uncertainty + authority + perspective + history + assumptions + limitations + transformations, and can reason about its own epistemic state.

unknown_candidate.why_uncertain: No existing index entry for a 'reflexive knowledge system' formalization; proposed as new, possibly part of the same overall object or a distinct one -- flagged here for orchestrator attention.

rows.statement: Defines an escalating series of knowledge-system representational completeness: a normal system represents K; a better one represents K+provenance(K); a trustworthy one represents K+provenance+uncertainty+authority; a reflexive knowledge system additionally represents K+provenance+uncertainty+authority+perspective+history+assumptions+limitations+transformations and can reason about its own epistemic state -- posed as KnowledgeOS's target formulation ('KnowledgeOS is a reflexive knowledge system').
missing: formal definitions of each added component (provenance, uncertainty, authority, perspective, history, assumptions, limitations, transformations)

rows.anchor: What happens when the system that knows becomes capable of examining how it knows? ... it should remain a reference model and diagnostic vocabulary, not become the architecture itself.

unknown_candidate.why_uncertain: Part of the same proposed object.

rows.statement: Closes with the open question 'what happens when the system that knows becomes capable of examining how it knows?' as the deepest connection to the KnowledgeOS program, paired with an explicit warning that the consciousness framework must remain a reference model and diagnostic vocabulary and never become the architecture itself.

rows.anchor: as a conceptual/epistemic analogy, not as a scientific claim that chakras physically exist or that knowledge literally has energy centres.
rows.statement: Explicitly frames the entire exercise as extracting an architectural pattern from the consciousness/chakra tradition as analogy, not asserting the tradition's mechanisms are literally real.

rows.anchor: Purusha | epistemic witness / meta-awareness ... I would not say KnowledgeOS has a 'soul'. Instead: Purusha becomes a useful metaphor for the observing layer that can distinguish the knowledge system from the contents of the knowledge system.
rows.statement: An 18-row correspondence table (Universe/Prakriti->knowledge environment, Senses->evidence acquisition, Nadis->information flows, Chakras->functional knowledge centres, Prana->epistemic flow, Manas->observation layer, Buddhi->reasoning, Ahamkara->perspective/bias, Samskaras->historical memory, Vasanas->persistent tendencies, Koshas->abstraction levels, Kundalini->progressive integration, Chakra blockage->knowledge debt/contradiction, Yoga->refinement practice, Dharana->focused investigation, Dhyana->sustained reasoning, Samadhi->integrated understanding, Purusha->epistemic witness/meta-awareness), with an explicit warning against reading Purusha as implying KnowledgeOS has a soul -- it is a metaphor for the layer distinguishing the knowledge system from its own contents.

rows.anchor: A document is not knowledge. It is closer to sensory input. A statement inside it is not necessarily truth. It is an observation or claim.
rows.statement: From the Manas(observation/capture)->Buddhi(interpretation/discrimination)->Ahamkara(perspective/ownership/bias)->Knowledge-State pipeline, derives the principle that a document is not knowledge but closer to sensory input, a statement inside it is an observation/claim rather than necessarily truth, and interpretation and perspective are separate operations layered on top.

rows.anchor: What was observed? -> What was inferred? -> What assumptions entered? -> What perspective entered? -> What alternatives exist? -> What contradicts it? -> What survives examination?
rows.statement: Frames critical thinking as the 'Buddhi-like' discrimination mechanism able to extract the state of knowledge, operationalized as a seven-question chain, and restates the Sankhya three-source-of-knowledge model (perception preferred, inference when perception insufficient, testimony when neither available) as an evidence pipeline: Direct observation / Inference / Authority-testimony -> Evaluation -> Knowledge State.
invariants: perception preferred over inference over testimony, in that priority order

rows.anchor: Knowledge Chakra 1 — Ground ... Knowledge Chakra 7 — Integration
rows.statement: Defines seven epistemic maturity stages (Ground: facts/observations/artifacts; Identity: entities/boundaries/terminology/ownership; Agency: causality/rules/dependencies/decisions; Relationship: relationships/contexts/trade-offs/conflicts/perspectives; Expression: language/definitions/models/contracts/documentation; Insight: inference/abstraction/analogy/principles/invariants; Integration: invariants/unifying principles/cross-domain understanding/meta-knowledge/epistemic boundaries), each keyed to a defining question, with the stated principle that if the Ground layer is unstable everything built above it is unstable, and knowledge that cannot be expressed precisely (Expression stage) cannot reliably be transferred.
invariants: instability at Ground propagates to all higher stages
knowledge inexpressible precisely cannot be reliably transferred

rows.anchor: A knowledge blockage at a lower level propagates upward. ... Ambiguous concept -> wrong model -> wrong architecture interpretation -> wrong decision -> wrong implementation -> false organizational knowledge
rows.statement: Catalogs ten knowledge-block types (missing evidence, contradictory evidence, ambiguous terminology, hidden assumption, obsolete decision, institutional bias, undocumented dependency, unresolved disagreement, ownership distortion, representation loss), asserts blockages at a lower maturity stage propagate upward, and gives a worked six-step failure chain from an ambiguous concept to false organizational knowledge, stated to be almost exactly the problem KnowledgeOS is trying to solve.
invariants: a knowledge blockage at a lower level propagates upward

rows.anchor: This is where I think we should not collapse the two models. Chakras and Koshas can represent different axes.
rows.statement: Proposes koshas (depth of representation: physical/operational/mental/wisdom/integrated) and chakras (functional dimension: Ground/Identity/Agency/Relation/Expression/Insight/Integration) as two independent, non-collapsible axes forming a 2-dimensional knowledge model (a depth x function matrix), explicitly warning against merging them into one hierarchy.
missing: worked example populating the 2D matrix with concrete content

rows.anchor: RAW KNOWLEDGE -> STABILIZED -> CONTEXTUALIZED -> CAUSAL -> RELATIONAL -> EXPLICIT -> INSIGHT -> INTEGRATED KNOWLEDGE ... It is not simply accumulation. It is transformation.
rows.statement: Reinterprets Kundalini's ascent from Muladhara to Sahasrara as a proposed 'Knowledge Evolution Path' (Raw -> Stabilized -> Contextualized -> Causal -> Relational -> Explicit -> Insight -> Integrated Knowledge), asserting the system does not merely accumulate knowledge but transforms.
invariants: knowledge evolution is transformation, not mere accumulation

rows.anchor: The highest epistemic state is not "knowing everything"; it is minimizing the distortions introduced by the separation between evidence, interpretation, model and observer.
rows.statement: Maps Yoga's eight limbs to a knowledge-development methodology (Yama->ethics, Niyama->discipline, Asana->stable structures, Pranayama->maintain flow, Pratyahara->remove noise, Dharana->focus on one epistemic question, Dhyana->sustained coherent reasoning, Samadhi->integrated understanding), and, reinterpreting the book's description of Dhyana (sustained uninterrupted stream) and Samadhi (removal of observer/process/object distinction), redefines the highest epistemic state as minimizing distortions from the separation between evidence, interpretation, model and observer -- identified as close to 'epistemic integrity'.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a system that maintains the evolving state of collective understanding.
rows.statement: Rejects the historical definition 'KnowledgeOS = repository + metadata + search + AI + governance' in favor of 'KnowledgeOS is a system that maintains the evolving state of collective understanding', modeled as a KNOWLEDGE CONSCIOUSNESS with three feeding branches -- MEMORY (evidence/history/experience/decisions), REASONING (Buddhi/inference/critique/synthesis), AWARENESS (meta-knowledge/uncertainty/perspective/blind spots) -- converging into a KNOWLEDGE STATE that splits into BLOCKS (contradictions/assumptions/ambiguity/bias) and GROWTH (integration/abstraction/insight/invariants).

lineage_claims.target: KnowledgeOS = repository + metadata + search + AI + governance
lineage_claims.quote: We have historically tended to think: KnowledgeOS = repository + metadata + search + AI + governance. This model suggests...

rows.anchor: K(t)=(E,C,I,A,P,R,U,B,M,S) where E=evidence, C=concepts, I=inferences, A=assumptions, P=perspectives, R=relationships, U=uncertainty, B=blocks/contradictions, M=models, S=stable/invariant knowledge
rows.statement: Rejects K={documents} as the state-of-knowledge model and instead defines the knowledge state at time t as a ten-component tuple K(t)=(E,C,I,A,P,R,U,B,M,S) (evidence, concepts, inferences, assumptions, perspectives, relationships, uncertainty, blocks/contradictions, models, stable/invariant knowledge).
missing: formal definition of each tuple component's type/domain

lineage_claims.quote: We don't want: K = {documents}. We want something more like: K(t)=(E,C,I,A,P,R,U,B,M,S)

rows.anchor: K_{t+1} = T(K_t, E_new, Contradictions, Questions) where T is the knowledge transformation process
rows.statement: Defines critical thinking as continuously performing a knowledge-state transition K_{t+1} = T(K_t, E_new, Contradictions, Questions), where T is termed 'the knowledge transformation process', operating on the K(t) tuple defined in the same file.

type_signature.domain: K_t x E_new x Contradictions x Questions

missing: definition of T

rows.anchor: The human system has both contents of consciousness and an observing consciousness. ... What do we know about what we know?
rows.statement: Reads Sankhya's Purusha (the 'Knower') vs Prakriti ('that which is known') distinction as a KnowledgeOS split between WHAT IS KNOWN (claims/evidence/models/decisions/history) and the KNOWING PROCESS (perception/inference/interpretation/evaluation/reflection), both feeding a META-KNOWLEDGE layer answering 'what do we know about what we know?', described as the point where KnowledgeOS becomes fundamentally different from a knowledge graph.

rows.anchor: A mature KnowledgeOS should not merely store knowledge. It should model the evolving consciousness of the knowledge system: what it observes, what it believes, why it believes it, what it does not know, what biases or assumptions shape it, where its knowledge is blocked, and what transformations are required to reach a more integrated and invariant understanding.
rows.statement: States the file's central research hypothesis (boxed): a mature KnowledgeOS must model the evolving 'consciousness' of the knowledge system itself -- what it observes, believes, why, what it doesn't know, its biases/assumptions, where it is blocked, and what transformations reach a more integrated/invariant understanding -- with the chakra/kosha/Sankhya/Yoga framework offered as a conceptual architecture for this hypothesis.

rows.anchor: We are not claiming that chakras, kundalini or prana are scientifically established mechanisms. We are extracting the structural theory from the tradition and asking whether its architecture can illuminate knowledge systems.
rows.statement: Explicit epistemic-boundary warning that the chakra/kundalini/prana mechanisms are not being asserted as scientifically established; only their structural theory is being extracted as a possible illuminating analogy.

rows.anchor: build a formal "Human Consciousness → Knowledge Consciousness" correspondence table, mapping Sankhya 25 tattvas + 5 koshas + 7 chakras + 8 yoga limbs against KnowledgeOS concepts, and then test which mappings are actually structurally valid rather than forcing an analogy.
rows.statement: Recommends as next step building a formal, testable correspondence table across the full Sankhya 25-tattva + 5-kosha + 7-chakra + 8-yoga-limb inventory against KnowledgeOS concepts, explicitly to test structural validity rather than force an analogy.

lexical.anchor: The consciousness model is not one architecture. It is a multi-lens model of a living system: what exists, how it is perceived, how it is interpreted, how identity forms around it, how action follows, how feedback changes the system, and how the system can become aware of its own knowing.

conceptual.anchor: It means every knowledge system has a standpoint problem.

formal.anchor: observation ≠ interpretation / interpretation ≠ inference / inference ≠ fact / testimony ≠ direct evidence / belief ≠ truth

assumption_register.statement: The consciousness model's functional separations can be repurposed to discover DDD bounded-context boundaries even though the source never frames them that way.
assumption_register.anchor: Not because the Sanskrit model says these are bounded contexts — it doesn't.

notations: r_i o T^-i = T o r_i

sources.note: Step 254's formal per-component removal test (r_i o T^-i = T o r_i) applied to the Step-230 kernel (K,C,T,E,A), proving component count != independent-primitive count; isolates the decisive provenance-at-t=0 counterexample refuting L=History(T) as a universal provenance account; redefines minimality as constrained optimization rather than cardinality; escalates 4 named normative decisions to the human author per the governing mandate.

rows.anchor: We need to distinguish three claims: Representable, Derivable, Primitive. They are not equivalent. If X=f(T) then X may be derivable. But that does not establish that X is unnecessary. Conversely, if X can be encoded inside T, that does not prove that the semantic concept represented by X can be eli
rows.statement: States a 3-way non-equivalence governing the whole removal-test methodology: Representable, Derivable, and Primitive are distinct claims, so encoding X inside another structure T neither proves X is unnecessary nor eliminates the semantic concept it represents.

rows.anchor: A component is removable only if there exists a reconstruction function r_i: K^-i -> K such that all required semantics are preserved. For every valid operation T, we require a commuting condition: r_i o T^-i = T o r_i. ... This is the formal version of the state-sufficiency criterion already develo
rows.statement: Formalizes the component-removal criterion as a commuting-diagram condition (r_i o T^-i = T o r_i for a reconstruction function r_i), explicitly identified as the same state-sufficiency congruence criterion developed in Step 248 (S1608), now applied component-wise rather than to the whole state abstraction.

rows.anchor: Minimality(K|T) not Minimality(K). ... if T2 superset T1 adds Merge, Supersede, Replay, ConflictResolution and provenance-sensitive operations, the same representation may cease to be sufficient. ... There may be no context-free minimal Knowledge State.
rows.statement: Reaffirms and applies Step 248's transformation-relative minimality principle (Minimality(K|T), not Minimality(K)) as the governing frame for the Step-254 removal tests, since expanding the transformation set can make a previously-sufficient representation insufficient.

rows.anchor: T mentioning K =/=> K derivable from T. Verdict: K is NOT shown removable. But importantly: K is also NOT proven primitive. ... C cannot currently be removed. But again: C is not thereby proven primitive. Context appears semantically necessary to some formulations, but its formal type remains unreso
rows.statement: Executes removal tests on K and C from the Step-230 kernel (K,C,T,E,A): K appearing inside T's signature does not prove K is derivable from T, so K is neither shown removable nor proven primitive; Context similarly cannot currently be removed (no established C=f(K,T,E,A) function, and any generic projection would silently pick one of Context's several overloaded meanings) but is also not thereby proven primitive.

rows.anchor: At t=0, external evidence may exist before any transformation occurs. Therefore Evidence_0 cannot generally be reconstructed from History(T) alone. This is structurally analogous to the provenance failure. Verdict: Evidence cannot presently be shown removable. ... there is no valid general function
rows.statement: Executes removal tests on Evidence and Authority: initial (t=0) external evidence cannot generally be reconstructed from History(T) alone (structurally analogous to the provenance base-case failure), so Evidence is not removable; Authority likewise has no general reconstruction function from the remaining components since it originates from an external actor/governance act (evidence, assessment and source do not self-authorize), so Authority is not removable either.

rows.anchor: T=f(K,C,E,A) ... The corpus explicitly warns that the theory cannot simultaneously claim T primitive and T=f(K,C,E,A) without specifying the direction of primitiveness. ... T may be primitive OR derived, but the corpus has not chosen. This is not a minor issue. It determines the ontology of the enti
rows.statement: Runs the reverse removal test on Transformation T itself, finding the corpus has never chosen a direction for T's primitiveness (T could be primitive, or derived as T=f(K,C,E,A)), and warns this ambiguity is not minor -- it determines the ontology of the entire kernel.

rows.anchor: At least four components appear inside the definition/signature of T. ... kernel independence classified as refuted for both Step 230 and Step 232. ... Kernel component count != number of independent primitives. A five-tuple is not automatically a five-primitive ontology.
rows.statement: States the central negative conclusion of the removal tests: since at least 4 of the 5 K230=(K,C,T,E,A) components appear inside T's own signature, kernel component count is not the same as the number of independent primitives -- a five-tuple candidate kernel is not automatically a five-primitive ontology, confirmed as refuted independence for both Step 230 and Step 232.

rows.anchor: History(T)=empty. Yet Provenance(H1) != Provenance(H2). Therefore History(T) cannot reconstruct all provenance. This is already recorded as a formal base-case failure. Provenance cannot be declared derived from T in general. This is one of the strongest findings in the entire reconstruction.
rows.statement: Gives the step's decisive counterexample: two initial histories with identical knowledge content but different externally-sourced evidence (e1 vs e2) both have History(T)=empty (no transformation has yet occurred) yet distinct Provenance, proving History(T) cannot universally reconstruct provenance -- named one of the strongest findings in the entire reconstruction.

experiment.hypothesis: Provenance can always be reconstructed as History(T).
experiment.setup: two initial states H1, H2 with identical knowledge content but different externally sourced evidence e1, e2.
experiment.assumptions: no transformation has yet occurred at t=0
experiment.method: compare History(T) and Provenance for both states at t=0
experiment.result: History(T) is empty for both, but Provenance(H1) != Provenance(H2)
experiment.interpretation: external/initial provenance is not a function of transformation history alone
experiment.conclusion: L=History(T) fails as a universal account of provenance

rows.anchor: Event=History(T) cannot automatically be universal [if events represent externally observed occurrences]. Event is not proven derivable from T. ... an observation cannot simply be reconstructed as 'whatever evidence exists.' ... Observation remains a live primitive candidate. ... Proposition has str
rows.statement: Runs further removal tests: Event is not proven derivable from T (externally observed events may exist independently of KnowledgeOS transformations); Observation cannot simply be reconstructed as evidence and remains a live primitive candidate; Proposition retains strong primitive status but its irreducibility is not proven, only that its removal is unjustified -- extending Step 253's (S1618) primitive audit with explicit removal-test rigor.

rows.anchor: Relation = structurally necessary candidate but Relation = primitive ontology is not established. ... if all relations are removed, the remaining objects become semantically disconnected ... Is Relation itself primitive, or is relation structure part of the mathematical representation of objects? Th
rows.statement: Runs the removal test for Relation, finding it structurally necessary (its removal disconnects all remaining objects semantically) but not established as primitive ontology, leaving open whether Relation is itself primitive or merely part of how mathematical structure represents objects -- consistent with Step 253's (S1618) ontological-vs-structural-primitive distinction.

rows.anchor: Transformation is the strongest historically supported kernel role [8/9]. We cannot yet say Transformation is mathematically primitive. ... Provenance in I* across all nine historical phases, yet it is absent from the latest kernels. Transformation: kernel-prominent, historically near-universal vers
rows.statement: Identifies a striking historical asymmetry: Transformation is the strongest historically-supported kernel role (present in 8 of 9 kernel candidates across the corpus's history) yet not proven mathematically primitive, while Provenance is the ONLY concept invariant across all 9 historical kernel phases (I*={Provenance}) yet is absent from the latest (Step 230/232) kernels -- historically-universal does not equal kernel-prominent, and vice versa; this asymmetry is a reason the current exclusion of Provenance cannot be justified by the History(T) argument, though it is not yet grounds to insert Provenance into the kernel.

rows.anchor: K* = argmin_{K_i} Complexity(K_i) subject to: forall T in T: F o That = T o F, and Identity, Provenance, Admissibility, History being preserved whenever the domain requires them. This is much stronger than the historical 'smallest tuple' approach. ... Mathematical minimality != smallest number of fi
rows.statement: Redefines the minimality target as a constrained optimization K*=argmin Complexity(K_i) subject to the congruence criterion holding for all transformations plus preservation of Identity/Provenance/Admissibility/History where required, explicitly rejecting cardinality (fewest fields) as a valid minimality criterion -- two models of equal or smaller size are not automatically better if they lose required semantics.

rows.anchor: Content-only: Falsified as universal candidate. Structured state (Content,Qualification,Governance,...): remains viable. History-inclusive state (State,Lineage,Provenance,...): also remains viable. No candidate has yet passed all requirements.
rows.statement: Consolidates candidate state representations into 3 groups: content-only is falsified as a universal candidate; a structured (Content,Qualification,Governance) model and a history-inclusive (State,Lineage,Provenance) model both remain viable, with neither yet passing all requirements -- narrowing but not resolving the architecture question.

rows.anchor: Lineage is insufficient as a universal substitute for provenance. It may still be sufficient for internal transformation lineage. That narrower claim survives. ... The Step-232 reconstruction ... fixed only one of nine properties and did not establish typing, determinism, composability, computabilit
rows.statement: Confirms lineage (History(T)) is insufficient as a universal substitute for provenance but remains sufficient for internal transformation lineage under explicit assumptions; separately notes Step 232's addition of Policy fixed only 1 of 9 required kernel properties (leaving typing, determinism, composability, computability, minimality, independence unaddressed) and that Policy being required for transformation-closure does not imply Policy is part of the Knowledge State -- governance may constrain transformations externally without becoming knowledge content.

rows.anchor: MINIMAL KERNEL NOT FOUND but also MINIMALITY TEST IS NOW FORMALLY SPECIFIED and THE FIRST IMPORTANT COUNTEREXAMPLE EXISTS: provenance at t=0. ... Semantic sufficiency -> congruence -> minimality, not: small tuple -> assumed sufficiency.
rows.statement: States the step's final verdict: no minimal kernel found, but the minimality test itself is now formally specified and a concrete counterexample (provenance at t=0) exists; reframes the correct methodological order as semantic-sufficiency-then-congruence-then-minimality, never starting from an assumed-sufficient small tuple.

rows.anchor: Decision 1 -- Is provenance semantically part of Knowledge? [Interpretation A: Provenance subseteq KnowledgeState; B: separate audit substrate] ... Decision 2 -- Must KnowledgeOS support exact historical reconstruction? [exact Replay vs observationally-equivalent] ... Decision 3 -- Is governance/aut
rows.statement: Invokes the governing mandate's escalation rule and stops to name 4 genuinely normative REQUIRES-USER-DECISION items with their alternative interpretations and consequences spelled out (provenance's constitutive status; exact vs observationally-equivalent replay; whether governance participates in semantic equality; which operations are mandatory, since minimality is relative to the transformation set), explicitly stating that without these decisions the mathematical attack can continue but no final minimal kernel can be legitimately declared.

rows.anchor: Step 255 -- State/History Congruence and Counterexample Catalogue ... construct explicit pairs (H1,H2) and systematically test F(H1)=F(H2) against every mandatory operation. The decisive experiment will be: F(H1)=F(H2) but T(H1)!=T(H2)? If such a case exists, state-only semantics fail.
rows.statement: Sets Step 255 as a systematic State/History Congruence and Counterexample Catalogue, requiring construction of history pairs and testing every mandatory operation against the congruence criterion, with the decisive falsification pattern being a pair where the state abstraction collapses (F(H1)=F(H2)) but a legitimate operation still distinguishes them (T(H1)!=T(H2)).

rows.anchor: That does not logically imply Provenance subseteq K. There are at least three possibilities: P subseteq K or P subseteq H or P subseteq ExternalAudit. The formal result is only: P must be preserved somewhere if provenance semantics are required. This is a much stronger and cleaner conclusion.
rows.statement: Resolves an apparent contradiction from S1620: proving provenance cannot be reconstructed from History(T) does NOT logically imply provenance must be inside K; instead 3 placements remain possible (inside K, inside H, or inside a separate external audit substrate), and the only proven result is that provenance must be preserved SOMEWHERE if provenance semantics are required -- a cleaner, weaker, and more defensible conclusion than the earlier framing.

rows.anchor: K should encode exactly the distinctions required by future semantics. Minimality = coarsest operationally valid equivalence. This is a much more powerful mathematical definition.
rows.statement: States the field-independent minimality reformulation: minimality equals the coarsest operationally valid equivalence on histories (K should encode exactly the distinctions required by future semantics, nothing more and nothing less), superseding the earlier 'how many fields' framing and directly instantiating S1620's constrained-optimization minimality target.

rows.anchor: Required(T) = StateReq(T) union ContextReq(T). Only StateReq(T) constrains K. ... K* = argmin_K Complexity(K) subject to semantic sufficiency.
rows.statement: Refines the kernel-minimization target by splitting an operation's total required information into StateReq(T) (must be resident in K) and ContextReq(T) (may be supplied externally, does not constrain K), restating the optimization target K*=argmin Complexity(K) subject to semantic sufficiency with this refined split.

rows.anchor: Does provenance belong in K? can now be answered experimentally. We do not ask philosophically. We ask: exists T: F(H1)=F(H2) but F(T_H(H1)) != F(T_H(H2))? If yes, F is insufficient. rows.anchor: The earlier candidate K=(K,C,T,E,A) should therefore be treated as a meta-structure, not automatically as the mathematical state itself. ... sources.note: Step 227 (tail, phase_measure_theory): proposes compressing the 182-step timeline into architectural eras/phases P_1..P_n (stable worldview intervals, transition when Worldview(P_i)!=Worldview(P_{i+1})), a 9-field per-phase profile, and a candidate 7-phase structure (Problem discovery -> Engineering system -> Knowledge externalization -> Governance & assurance -> Mathematical formalization -> Semantic architecture -> Knowledge transformation/KnowledgeOS) explicitly requiring phase boundaries to come from historical evidence, not the proposed outline.

rows.anchor: P_1,P_2,\ldots,P_n such that within each phase the underlying architectural worldview is relatively stable. ... Worldview(P_i)\neq Worldview(P_{i+1}).
rows.statement: Step 227 (tail) proposes compressing the 182-step timeline into architectural-era phases P_1..P_n, each an interval of relatively stable underlying architectural worldview, with a phase transition defined as Worldview(P_i) != Worldview(P_{i+1}).

rows.anchor: 1. dominant problem; ... 9. unresolved contradictions. ... PHASE I Problem discovery ... PHASE VII Knowledge transformation / KnowledgeOS ... the phase boundaries must come from the historical evidence -- not from this proposed outline.
rows.statement: Per-phase profile schema (9 fields: dominant problem, dominant architectural model, key concepts, dominant evidence type, implementation maturity, governance maturity, mathematical formalization, Gita relationship, unresolved contradictions) and a candidate 7-phase structure (I Problem discovery, II Engineering system, III Knowledge externalization, IV Governance & assurance, V Mathematical formalization, VI Semantic architecture, VII Knowledge transformation/KnowledgeOS) -- explicitly requiring that phase boundaries be derived from historical evidence, not from this proposed outline, as the next major test of whether the current architecture is genuinely a result of Steps 1-182 or a compelling retrospective theory.

rows.anchor: W_i \not\approx W_{i+1} where the difference is significant enough to change architecture, not merely terminology. TerminologyChange\neq ArchitecturalTransition.
rows.statement: Formal phase-transition definition: a phase transition occurs when the architectural worldview W_i is not approximately equal to W_{i+1}, with the difference significant enough to change architecture rather than merely terminology -- TerminologyChange != ArchitecturalTransition.

rows.anchor: 1. Problem redefinition ... 10. New verification mechanism. A single new feature is normally insufficient.
rows.statement: A genuine phase transition should satisfy several of ten conditions (problem redefinition, new architectural boundary, new invariant, new artifact type, new governance mechanism, new evidence model, new mathematical formalization, new human/AI relationship, new understanding of knowledge, new verification mechanism); a single new feature alone is normally insufficient.

rows.anchor: Phase I -- Software/Problem Construction ... Phase VIII -- Knowledge Transformation Architecture
rows.statement: Candidate 8-phase model (explicitly not yet historical conclusions): PI Software/Problem Construction (W1: build working software; concern Functionality), PII Engineering System (W2: software developed within an engineering system: Code+Process+Architecture+Decisions+Constraints), PIII Knowledge Externalization (W3: engineering reasoning itself is an architectural asset; Artifact!=Knowledge, e.g. ADR!=DecisionKnowledge), PIV Governed Knowledge (W4: knowledge must be governed to remain trustworthy; introduces Authority/Provenance/Lifecycle/Governance), PV Assurance (W5: knowledge and transformations must be verifiable; chain Requirement->Invariant->Implementation->Check->Evidence), PVI Formal/Mathematical Architecture, PVII Semantic Architecture, PVIII Knowledge Transformation Architecture.

rows.anchor: P(X\in A) ... F_X(x) ... \hat F_n(x) ... H(X) ... D(P\parallel Q). These are useful formalization tools. They do not automatically constitute architecture.
rows.statement: Phase VI candidate mathematical structures: probability P(X in A), distribution F_X(x)=P(X<=x), empirical distribution hat F_n(x), Shannon entropy H(X)=-sum p(x)log p(x), and KL-divergence D(P||Q)=sum P(x)log(P(x)/Q(x)) -- flagged as useful formalization tools that do not automatically constitute architecture.

rows.anchor: MathematicalModel from ArchitecturalInvariant ... Formalism\neq Architecture. Formalism supports architecture.
rows.statement: Critical distinction: MathematicalModel != ArchitecturalInvariant -- e.g. D(P||Q) can measure distributional divergence but the architectural rule ('a transformation must not introduce an unacknowledged semantic change') is not the mathematical measure itself; boxed as Formalism != Architecture (formalism supports architecture, it is not architecture).

rows.anchor: Correctness\neq SemanticIntegrity. ... What meaning must survive a transformation? This creates SemanticBoundary and SemanticInvariant.
rows.statement: Phase VII (Semantic Architecture) is triggered by recognizing that a transformation may be technically valid while changing meaning: Correctness != SemanticIntegrity, producing the concepts SemanticBoundary and SemanticInvariant around the question of what meaning must survive a transformation.

rows.anchor: R_C(K_A)\subseteq Recoverable(T(K_A)). If something is intentionally lost, Loss(T) must be explicit. This is one of the most promising mathematical foundations for the emerging architecture.
rows.statement: Semantic preservation condition restated for a transformation T:K_A->K_B and context-specific semantic projection R_C(K): R_C(K_A) subseteq Recoverable(T(K_A)), with any intentional loss Loss(T) required to be explicit -- rated one of the most promising mathematical foundations for the emerging architecture.

rows.anchor: Transformation(K_A,K_B,C,A,P) ... T=(Input,Context,Authority,Preconditions,Operation,Postconditions,PreservationRules,Evidence).
rows.statement: Phase VIII candidate architecture: the central object becomes Transformation(K_A,K_B,C,A,P) (source knowledge, resulting knowledge, context, authority, provenance) rather than Knowledge itself, formalized as a transformation contract T=(Input,Context,Authority,Preconditions,Operation,Postconditions,PreservationRules,Evidence), applicable across AI generation, code generation, architecture transformation, document transformation, knowledge extraction, governance decisions, and model transformations.

rows.anchor: GOVERNANCE / TRANSFORMATION Contract+Rules / Verification / Provenance / Evidence diagram
rows.statement: The emerging candidate architecture diagram: Governance (Authority/Policy) sits above a Transformation node (Contract+Rules) connecting Knowledge Context A to Knowledge Context B, with the transformation feeding both Verification and Provenance, both converging on Evidence -- rated a strong candidate architecture still requiring historical validation.

rows.anchor: P_{n+1}\supseteq P_n ... NewPhase=PreviousCapabilities+NewWorldview.
rows.statement: Important correction to the phase model: phase transitions are not necessarily linear replacement (P_1->P_2->...->P_8 does not mean earlier concerns disappear); instead P_{n+1} superset-or-equal P_n is a better model, giving NewPhase = PreviousCapabilities + NewWorldview -- e.g. a semantic-architecture phase still requires software engineering, governance, testing, deployment, security, infrastructure.

rows.anchor: L_1=Software ... L_8=Transformation. A=\bigcup_{i=1}^{8}L_i subject to compatibility constraints.
rows.statement: Layered evolution model: the architecture is viewed as 8 accumulated layers L1=Software, L2=Engineering, L3=Knowledge, L4=Governance, L5=Assurance, L6=Formalization, L7=Semantics, L8=Transformation, with A = union of L_i for i=1..8 subject to compatibility constraints.

rows.anchor: Governance may have existed from the beginning. ... FirstExplicitAppearance versus FirstImplicitPresence. These are not the same.
rows.statement: Danger flagged in the layered interpretation: some 'phases' (e.g. Governance, Knowledge) may not be genuine later phases at all but implicit from Step 1; the historical audit must distinguish FirstExplicitAppearance from FirstImplicitPresence, which are not the same.

rows.anchor: t_E(c)=first explicit occurrence ... t_I(c)=earliest defensible implicit occurrence. ... t_I(c)\leq t_E(c). The interval [t_I,t_E] represents the period during which the concept may have been present but unnamed.
rows.statement: Explicit-vs-implicit architecture formalism: for concept c, t_E(c) = first explicit occurrence and t_I(c) = earliest defensible implicit occurrence, with t_I(c) <= t_E(c); the interval [t_I,t_E] represents the period during which the concept may have been present but unnamed -- especially important for semantic concepts.

rows.anchor: implementation -> repeated constraint -> observed pattern -> named principle -> formal invariant. ... Implementation\rightarrow Concept\rightarrow Formalization may be historically more accurate than Concept\rightarrow Implementation.
rows.statement: Architecture often precedes vocabulary: a system can enforce an invariant before anyone names it, following the pattern implementation -> repeated constraint -> observed pattern -> named principle -> formal invariant; the historically more accurate general order may be Implementation -> Concept -> Formalization rather than the assumed Concept -> Implementation.

rows.anchor: We should not merely search for the first occurrence of words such as: knowledge; provenance; semantic; ... We must search for the behavioral pattern represented by those concepts.
rows.statement: Consequence for interpreting Steps 1-182: the audit must not merely search for first occurrences of terminology (knowledge, provenance, semantic, governance, assurance, transformation) but for the underlying behavioral pattern -- an early history-preserving mechanism may constitute an early form of temporal lineage even if nobody named it that.

rows.anchor: Pass A -- lexical ... Pass B -- structural ... LexicalAppearance with StructuralAppearance. This can reveal hidden architectural continuity.
rows.statement: The audit requires two passes: Pass A lexical (find explicit terminology) and Pass B structural (find the behavior/reasoning corresponding to the concept), comparing LexicalAppearance against StructuralAppearance to reveal hidden architectural continuity -- applied identically to the Gita chapter analysis (structural themes: Ch1 Conflict->Uncertainty->NeedForOrientation, Ch2 Identity+Change+Discernment, Ch3 Action+Duty+Consequences, Ch4 Knowledge+Action+Transmission+Continuity), explicitly labeled interpretive mappings, not technical evidence.

rows.anchor: Architecture\leftarrow EngineeringEvidence and Gita\rightarrow InterpretiveReflection. The two can converge without one being falsely claimed as the source of the other.
rows.statement: The correct architecture-Gita relationship is EngineeringHistory + MathematicalFormalization + PhilosophicalReflection, not EngineeringHistory = Gita; formalized as Architecture <- EngineeringEvidence and Gita -> InterpretiveReflection as two convergent but independently-sourced streams.

rows.anchor: Conflict\rightarrow Discernment\rightarrow Action\rightarrow Knowledge ... resonates with Problem\rightarrow Analysis\rightarrow Decision\rightarrow Execution\rightarrow Learning. But the book should label this as StructuralCorrespondence unless historical causality is demonstrated.
rows.statement: A possible deeper correspondence between a Gita-derived philosophical pattern (Conflict->Discernment->Action->Knowledge) and an engineering pattern (Problem->Analysis->Decision->Execution->Learning) must be labeled StructuralCorrespondence, not causal derivation, unless historical causality is demonstrated.

rows.anchor: \Theta(P_i,P_{i+1}) based on: problem change; concept change; ... We should not pretend this is a scientifically calibrated numerical probability. It is an audit instrument.
rows.statement: A qualitative phase-transition-evidence score Theta(P_i,P_{i+1}) is defined over seven change dimensions (problem, concept, invariant, boundary, implementation, governance, verification change), explicitly not a scientifically calibrated numerical probability but an audit instrument.

rows.anchor: Confidence(TP)=\{High,Medium,Low\}. A transition is High only when several independent signals support it.

aliases: Master Research Handoff -- Representation Reduction Under Preservation Contracts

sources.note: The 2026-09-03 master research handoff establishing the KnowledgeOS representation-reduction theory as the successor to KR-ZERO: formalizes a preservation contract Pi=(Q,C,O) (inquiry, admissibility constraints, decoder), an admissible domain X_{Pi,T}={D: C(T(D))=1}, adequacy H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 with the population-vs-empirical-adequacy distinction (H_hat vs H) kept explicit, a structural fiber-violation count N_viol(R) shown equivalent to H_hat(Q|R)=0 on finite empirical support, an information-theoretic-excess quantity H(T|Q) relabelled 'inquiry-extraneous relative to Q' (never 'objectively superfluous'), three theorems (Theorem 1 adequacy iff an optimal decoder exists; Theorem 2 factorization/fiber preservation Q=O*∘T on the admissible domain, explicitly NOT a bijection without further proof; Theorem 3 an information lower bound H(T*)>=H(Q) with equality iff H(T|Q)=0), a Contractually Eliminable Set Elim_{T,Pi}(D) defined without assuming E_S(D)=D\S, the general non-element-wise Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D), and the new research object 𝒵(D,S,R,I,C,M,T,Π,W) / 𝒦_Π=(X,𝒯,𝓔,~_Π,Q). Reports the actual KR-ZERO-ORDER-2026-09 higher-order-Zero experiment's published aggregate (k=1: 1252/1395=89.7%, k=2: 25/1395=1.8%, k=3: 3/1395=0.2%, irreducible: 115/1395=8.24%; per-transformation interaction rates T1..T8 ranging 0%-31.46%; monotonicity 387/391), and issues a critical warning that the old KR-ZERO experiment's R1-R4 representation-CLASS labels (token/token+metadata/graph/structured-claim) must never be treated as levels of a new R5->R4->R3->R2->R1 sequential REDUCTION hierarchy -- a 'dangerous naming collision' with zero corpus evidence for any such hierarchy -- mandating a new experiment KR-REP-REDUCTION-2026-09 with ten research-discipline rules (never infer a hierarchy from naming alone; never fabricate missing case-level data; separate empirical from theoretical claims; persist the full population, never only failures/witnesses) and a six-phase Claude Code CLI audit protocol (Inventory -> Classify -> Verify old KR-ZERO -> Protect against R1-R4 collision -> Theory-to-corpus gap matrix -> new experiment design) before any implementation.

rows.anchor: How much representation can be eliminated while remaining in the same inquiry-relevant equivalence class and satisfying the preservation contract? ... This is NOT fundamentally a question about digit count.
rows.statement: States the central research question of the new phase in general form (not the '5-digit to 2-digit' motivating example): given source representation D, inquiry Q, constraints C, decoder O, and transformation family T, how far can representation be reduced before preservation fails; formalizes the preservation contract as Pi=(Q,C,O) and the admissible domain X_{Pi,T}={D: C(T(D))=1}.

rows.anchor: H_hat(Q|R)=0 means no observed R-fiber contains conflicting Q values. This is evidence about the observed population, not proof of generalization to an unseen population.
rows.statement: States Theorem 1 (adequacy H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 iff an optimal decoder O* exists with P(O*(T(D))=Q(D))=1) and mandates that empirical adequacy (H_hat, measured on a finite dataset) must never be silently promoted to theoretical/population adequacy (H); defines the structural audit N_viol(R)=#{(Da,Db): R(Da)=R(Db) and Q(Da)!=Q(Db)}, shown equivalent to H_hat(Q|R)=0 under the standard empirical distribution, to be reported alongside the entropy summary.

rows.anchor: H(T) = H(Q) + H(T|Q) ... Do NOT call this objectively superfluous information. Correct terminology: inquiry-extraneous representation relative to Q.
rows.statement: States Theorem 2 (Q factors through T on the admissible domain, Q-factorized/Q-equivalent, explicitly not automatically a bijection) and Theorem 3 (an information lower bound H(T*)>=H(Q) for T* minimizing entropy among adequate transformations, with equality iff H(T|Q)=0), deriving the central decomposition H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q) and insisting the excess term H(T|Q) be called 'inquiry-extraneous representation relative to Q,' never 'objectively superfluous,' since extraneousness is contract-relative.

rows.anchor: Elim_{T,Pi}(D) = {S: D in X_{Pi,T} and E_S(D) in X_{Pi,T} and O(T(D))=O(T(E_S(D)))=Q(D)} ... Zero(a1;D) AND Zero(a2;D) does NOT imply Zero({a1,a2};D).
rows.statement: Defines the Contractually Eliminable Set Elim_{T,Pi}(D) without assuming the naive E_S(D)=D\S elimination operator, and generalizes Zero to a subset-relative, non-element-wise predicate Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), citing the deduplication witness D=[a,a,b,b] where individual occurrences are eliminable but eliminating both occurrences of a simultaneously changes the representation -- concluding eliminability may be relational and Zero must remain defined over subsets/groups where appropriate.

Reports the published aggregate of the higher-order-Zero experiment KR-ZERO-ORDER-2026-09: of 1,395 cases, 89.7% resolve at interaction order k=1, 1.8% at k=2, 0.2% at k=3, and 8.24% are irreducible; per-transformation interaction rates vary sharply (T2 dedup 31.46%, T8 interacting 20.59%, T4 context 11.50%, T1/T5/T7 0%, T3/T6 <1%); and monotonicity of interaction order in subset size holds in 387 of 391 tested cases but is explicitly NOT a universal law, so the conclusion 'Zero is fundamentally higher-order' must not be drawn from a non-negligible but minority irreducible class.

rows.anchor: R1, R2, R3, R4 ... are REPRESENTATION CLASSES. They are NOT R5 -> R4 -> R3 -> R2 -> R1 reduction levels. There is a dangerous naming collision.
rows.statement: Issues a critical, explicitly labelled warning against a naming collision: the old KR-ZERO experiment's R1-R4 labels denote representation CLASSES (token sequence, token sequence+metadata, graph/relational, structured claim/evidence), independently sampled with no R_n->R_{n-1} transformation between them, and must never be reinterpreted as levels of the new sequential R5->R4->R3->R2->R1 reduction hierarchy; a grep/audit found zero evidence in the old KR-ZERO corpus for Q(D), R5, C(Rn), O(Rn), representation_hierarchy, or reduction_level, so KR-ZERO-ORDER != KR-REP-DATASET.

rows.anchor: RULE 1: Inspect before hypothesizing. ... RULE 10: Persist the full experimental population.
rows.statement: States a ten-rule research discipline for the new KR-REP-REDUCTION-2026-09 experiment (inspect before hypothesizing; never infer a hierarchy from naming alone; never fabricate missing case-level data; separate old experiments from new theoretical constructs; separate empirical results from mathematical claims; separate adequacy from realization; separate entropy from representation size/capacity; never assume algebraic structure before proving/observing it; preserve negative results and falsifications; persist the full experimental population, never only failures/witnesses/aggregates), and specifies a six-phase Claude Code audit protocol (A Inventory, B Classify Artifacts, C Verify Old KR-ZERO, D Protect Against R1-R4 Collision, E Theory-to-Corpus Gap matrix with status vocabulary IMPLEMENTED/PARTIAL/EMPIRICALLY TESTED/THEORETICAL ONLY/ABSENT/CONFLICTING, F New Experiment Design) that must produce a first-response inventory-classify-verify-map-design report BEFORE any implementation, explicitly rejecting an ASSUME->ADAPT->FABRICATE sequence.

rows.anchor: Last adequate stage: R5. First inadequate: R4. Crossing transformation: T4 -- rounding to 3 significant digits. ... TEST reproduces TRAIN closely
rows.statement: Reports the located adequacy boundary (R5 adequate at Hhat=0, R4 inadequate at Hhat=0.4299) reproduced closely on an independent test split (0.4408 vs 0.4299), confirming it is not a one-sample artifact.

rows.anchor: GoF can support the engineering of that experiment, but GoF should not be used as the theory that proves the result. ... So GoF is underneath the research theory, not above it.
rows.statement: States the governing relationship for the representation-reduction experiment: KnowledgeOS Theory (Preservation Contract Pi, Adequacy H(Q|R), Fiber Preservation, Realization F(R), Information Excess H(R|Q), Reduction Boundary) sits above the research experiment, which splits into mathematical definitions and an engineering implementation; GoF patterns belong only to the engineering-implementation branch, never to the theory branch.

rows.anchor: Strategy implements T_n; it does not define what T_n means epistemically. ... ReductionStrategy: T5,T4,T3,T2,T1 ... lets the experiment substitute transformations without changing the experimental controller.
rows.statement: Proposes GoF Strategy to implement the D->R5->R4->R3->R2 chain's transformations T5..T1 as interchangeable ReductionStrategy implementations, explicitly separating implementing T_n from defining T_n's epistemic meaning.

rows.anchor: GoF Strategy or Adapter could implement different decoder/operator interfaces ... The research determines whether O(R_n)=Q(D) actually holds.
rows.statement: Proposes Strategy/Adapter for implementing multiple decoder/operator (O5, O4, O3, ...) interfaces over a representation, while the empirical/mathematical question of whether a given operator actually realizes Q(D)=O(R_n) remains outside GoF's scope.

rows.anchor: GoF Template Method is useful here. ReductionExperiment: generate(), transform(), evaluateContract(), evaluateAdequacy(), evaluateRealization(), measure(), persist() ... particularly appropriate because your document explicitly requires the same metric vector at every reduction stage.
rows.statement: Proposes GoF Template Method for the fixed seven-step experiment pipeline (generate/transform/evaluateContract/evaluateAdequacy/evaluateRealization/measure/persist), matching the handoff's requirement of an identical metric vector at every reduction stage.

rows.anchor: the carrier is still an unresolved research question: subset, relational structure, graph/hypergraph, rewriting state, structured representation, combinations ... not to assume the carrier before experimentation. This is an excellent place for GoF Adapter. ... Adapter must not be interpreted as evidence that these carriers are semantically equivalent. It merely allows the experiment to compare them.
rows.statement: Proposes GoF Adapter (SequenceAdapter/GraphAdapter/StructureAdapter) to let the experiment evaluate multiple unresolved candidate representation carriers through a common interface, with an explicit warning that using Adapter must not be read as evidence the carriers are semantically equivalent -- it only enables comparison.

rows.anchor: Where GoF should NOT be used ... What Zero means [not a GoF design-pattern question] ... Whether R2 is adequate H(Q|R2)=0 [an information-theoretic/empirical question, GoF has nothing to say] ... Whether the representation boundary is real [part of the research semantics, GoF cannot prove any of those boundaries] ... Whether a transformation is mathematically valid [algebraic structure, projection properties, idempotence, commutativity -- a GoF pattern does not establish any of those properties]
rows.statement: Enumerates four questions GoF categorically cannot answer for the representation-reduction research: the definition of Zero, the adequacy of R2 (H(Q|R2)=0), the reality of the representation/contract/operator boundaries, and the mathematical validity (algebraic structure, idempotence, commutativity) of any transformation.

rows.anchor: For the attached R5 -> R2 experiment (research-element-to-GoF-role table): D->R_n = Strategy; different transformation families = Strategy/Factory; fixed experiment pipeline = Template Method; different representation carriers = Adapter; representation traversal = Iterator/Composite; experiment command/audit record = Command; snapshot before transformation = Memento; experiment coordination = Facade/Mediator; dataset construction = Builder/Factory; test-case variants = Prototype; contract/metrics/H(Q|R)/fiber preservation/Zero/minimal adequate representation/reduction boundary = NOT GoF.
rows.statement: Provides a complete research-element-to-GoF-role allocation table for the R5->R2 experiment, explicitly marking six theory-level elements (contract/metrics, H(Q|R), fiber preservation, Zero, minimal adequate representation, reduction boundary) as NOT GoF -- belonging to KnowledgeOS theory, information theory, mathematics, or empirical results instead.

rows.anchor: H0: The proposed KnowledgeOS representation-reduction mechanism is completely implementable as ordinary composition of established GoF patterns without introducing a semantically new primitive. ... This is very valuable, because it prevents KnowledgeOS from inventing new primitives merely because an implementation feels novel.
rows.statement: Formulates a falsifiable H0 hypothesis that the representation-reduction mechanism is fully implementable as composition of Strategy/Template-Method/Adapter/Iterator/Composite/Command without a new semantic primitive, framed as a safeguard against inventing primitives from implementation novelty alone.

experiment.hypothesis: The KnowledgeOS representation-reduction mechanism is completely implementable as ordinary composition of established GoF patterns without a new semantic primitive.

If the gap was already empty, then a valid inquiry-preserving transformation can maintain Delta(T(K_t))=empty. So Zero can function as a preserved semantic condition, not merely as a terminal numerical value.

rows.anchor: Presentation = Epistemically\ Qualified\ Projection
rows.statement: Deeper DDD point: Present() must not be understood as 'turn database objects into UI' but as a semantic projection that decides what is relevant, critical, uncertain, conflicting, missing, evidenced, recommendation-vs-fact, and inference-vs-observation. Presentation = Epistemically Qualified Projection.

rows.anchor: \Pi_{N,D,P,C,F}
rows.statement: New concept: Presentation Projection Π_{N,D,P,C,F} parameterized by Knower N, Decision D, Purpose P, Context C, Format F, giving P_t = Π_{N,D,P,C,F}(S_t). Enables two different Knowers to receive different presentations of the same underlying state without KnowledgeOS holding two different Knowledge States.

rows.anchor: CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) \subseteq Preserved(P_t)
rows.statement: Presentation is loss-aware: as a projection it may lose information but must not lose epistemically important distinctions — e.g. Observed/Reported/Inferred/Assumed must not all collapse into 'FACT', and Strong/Weak/No evidence must not all collapse into 'CONFIDENT'. Defines EpistemicFidelity(P_t,S_t) and requires CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) ⊆ Preserved(P_t) as one of the most important invariants of the presentation architecture.

rows.statement: Corrects the earlier O_core formulation's category error: operations belong to different mathematical categories (Assert changes state, Query observes, Compare produces a relation, Authorize evaluates governance admissibility, Serialize changes representation, Replay reconstructs history) and must not be treated as one homogeneous algebra. Defines the full operation universe as a union of five disjoint families: semantic-state, observation, governance, historical, and representation.

rows.statement: Derives the candidate semantic operation universe as the union of five families: semantic state operations O_S = {Assert, Retract, Supersede, Infer, Merge}; evidence/epistemic operations O_E = {Support, Refute, Qualify, Assess, DetectContradiction, Resolve}; observation/equivalence operations O_O = {Query, Compare, Identity, Equal}; historical operations O_H = {Replay, Trace}; governance operations O_G = {Authorize, Validate}. Representation/infrastructure operations (Serialize, Deserialize, Save, Load, Delete) are explicitly excluded from the semantic kernel (O_repr ∩ O_sem = ∅).

rows.anchor: It would be incorrect to infer: $$Operation\rightarrow StateField$$ For example: $$DetectContradiction$$ does not imply: $$Conflict\in\Sigma$$ as a primitive field. Likewise: $$Supersede$$ does not imply: $$Superseded\in\Sigma.$$
rows.statement: Names one of the step's most important conclusions: an operation existing in O_core does not imply the distinction it detects must become a primitive field of Sigma. DetectContradiction existing does not force Conflict into Sigma; Supersede existing does not force Superseded into Sigma; Replay existing does not force complete history to be embedded in K. Operations constrain K but do not dictate its decomposition — hence a genuine sufficiency/minimality proof (not operation enumeration) is still required for K and Sigma.

rows.anchor: ### F272A-1 — Missing mandatory operation ... F272A-2 — Redundant operation ... F272A-3 — Category error ... F272A-4 — Hidden dependency ... F272A-5 — Governance contamination ... F272A-6 — Historical contamination
rows.statement: Specifies six falsification requirements the candidate operation universe must survive: (1) remove each candidate operation and test whether a mandatory distinction becomes impossible; (2) attempt to express each operation via the remaining operations (redundancy test); (3) test whether an operation actually belongs to another semantic layer (e.g. verify Serialize is not in O_sem); (4) determine whether an operation requires information not represented by candidate K (hidden dependency); (5) verify Authorize does not become an epistemic-status transition merely because it gates permitted transformations; (6) verify Replay does not require history to be treated as an instantaneous state component.

rows.statement: Twelve concepts projected into PublicDigit, a hypothetical Hospital Information System, and a hypothetical ERP System: MISSION, STRATEGY, DESIGN POLICY, CAPABILITY, KNOWLEDGE, ARTIFACT, KNOWLEDGE SPACE, PRODUCT are invariant across all three; PRINCIPLE specializes (partly external in Hospital and ERP, owned by a regulator/accounting standard); PKS fails (one per product, or per deployment?); RUNTIME ADAPTER disappears in both new domains; PROJECTION (I-4) fails, since a discharge summary and a financial statement are both generated and legally/formally authoritative.

experiment.hypothesis: The relationship ontology's twelve concepts and eleven invariants hold unchanged when projected into unrelated product domains.
experiment.setup: The ontology was held fixed and conceptually (no implementation) projected into three domains: PublicDigit (actual), a hypothetical Hospital Information System, and a hypothetical ERP System, examining each concept and invariant for survival.
experiment.assumptions: the hypothetical domains are represented faithfully enough by their described contexts, invariants, design policies, bindings and authorities
experiment.inputs: domain sketches for PublicDigit, Hospital, ERP (contexts, core invariant, a design policy, a binding, authority)
experiment.method: concept-by-concept and invariant-by-invariant projection and comparison across the three domains
experiment.result: 8 of 12 concepts and 10 of 11 invariants survived unchanged; PRINCIPLE and PKS required specialization; RUNTIME ADAPTER disappeared in the two new domains; I-4 was falsified.
experiment.interpretation: the ontology is largely domain-independent but has a systemic gap: it can express structure but not transformation (specialization, external constraint, instantiation, attestation).
experiment.limitations: the Hospital and ERP domains are hypothetical, not implemented or independently reviewed
experiment.conclusion: the ontology survives projection but not unchanged; PublicDigit itself masked two of the three failures (multi-tenancy, external legal authority).
